fields.AN_Notes: Reflexive thematic analysis of FAccT and AIES papers on intersectionality, evaluated in a workshop with AI experts; the result is a set of recommendations for AI experts. The workshop assessed perceived actionability, not the effect of a mitigation on bias, so the status stays Proposed. Harm types: the welfare fraud cases (Netherlands, France), Gender Shades and COMPAS are cited cases and illustrations from other work; the work's own argument concerns the narrow algorithmic frame of AI fairness and establishes no harm mechanism of its own, hence None. Bias axes: Gender, Race_Ethnicity and Intersectional from the work's own worked example of Black women (introduction) and its intersectional subgroup argument (4.2.2); dual nationality and low-income or immigrant background appear only in the cited welfare cases and stay uncoded. Gender understanding: the work states race as socially constructed (footnote 1, 4.4.3) but makes no such statement about gender, so Social_Construct is not coded. Soziale_Arbeit teilweise rests on the welfare benefits cases used as opening motivation. AN_Task None: the work addresses AI development practice, not a task in which AI is used.

fields.AN_Notes: Conceptual paper that rearticulates the seven data feminism principles for AI research and proposes two further principles (environment, consent); the appendix calls it primarily a literature review and theory contribution, coded Konzept because the principles form a framework. Other_Axis: colonial Global North/Global South position, argued in Principle 7 (labour hierarchy) and 5.1 (environmental impact). Harm types: Exclusionary_Norms for the gender binary operationalised in AI research (4.3), Erasure for missing data on groups and the erasure of trans and non-binary people (4.1, 4.3), Indirect_Discrimination for tenant screening on eviction records, arrest records and credit scores that disproportionately impacts people of color (4.1); harms such as Gender Shades, LAION misogyny or anti-Muslim LLM bias are cited from other work and left uncoded. Mitigation: collection of missing data on underrepresented people (Pre_Processing) and participatory methods, AI education, regulation and collective action (Organisational_Process), all proposed. Bias is not determined in a sentence of its own; the understanding of bias as a product of unequal social relations is recognisable from the frame (Implicit_Only). Fairness nein: the paper frames its argument as justice and power, not as algorithmic fairness criteria or metrics.

fields.AN_Notes: Systematic review of social work and AI scholarship with qualitative content analysis, structured by Staub-Bernasconi's triple mandate, and a proposed Unified Model for AI Enhanced Social Work. Bias axes None: indigenous peoples, younger people and the poor appear only as a one-sentence enumeration from cited studies in the synthesis theme 'Data and Algorithmic Injustice'. Harm types: Erasure is coded because that synthesis theme of the review rests on under-representation that makes groups invisible; the other consequences listed there (exclusion, stigmatization, discrimination) are named from cited studies without a mechanism, and no allocation-based discrimination is established. Mitigation: inclusive data sets (Pre_Processing) and governance, participation, interdisciplinary teams and training (Organisational_Process), proposed. Tasks synthesised: decision support and risk assessment, organisational quality control and resource allocation, research use of text mining. Bias is not determined; the understanding as discrimination contrary to human rights is recognisable from the nondiscrimination frame (Implicit_Only). Gender is not treated.

fields.AN_Notes: Qualitative interpretative visual analysis of 180 Stable Diffusion XL images from minimal prompts along privilege and disadvantage, ideology and everyday scenarios, followed by a micro, meso and macro intersectional analysis. Prompting is the research instrument; the only prompting recommendation is that users be more conscious of what kind of prompts they use, with no codable technique (AN_Prompt_Techniques None). Religion was deliberately excluded from the prompts and is not coded. Harm types from the work's own image analysis: Stereotyping (darker skin tones tied to criminality, own named harm), Exclusionary_Norms (white, able-bodied, heteronormative masculine default), Erasure (absence of non-binary and disabled representations), Misrepresentation (reductionist portrayal of cultural contexts, Global South shown only as impoverished). The less accurate depiction of dishes such as fufu concerns cultural items rather than a quality difference between social groups and is not coded as Disparate_Performance. Gender definition Explicit rests on footnote 2, which determines the binary gender norm and replaces man and woman by heteronormative feminine and masculine representations. Mitigation: better training data curation, more conscious prompting by users, regulation, criminal culpability, team diversity and algorithmic reparation, all proposed. AN_Task None: the work audits a general image generator without an application task of professional practice.
